node-1.label: Patient presented to the emergency department with complaints of dizziness

node-2.label: Patient in their 70s with history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and structurally normal heart was prescribed flecainide 100 mg twice a day for rhythm control

node-3.label: Physical examination: blood pressure 60/44 mm Hg, heart rate 166 beats/min, oxygen saturation 100% on ambient air

why.why: The laboratory physician analysis explicitly supports supraventricular tachycardia with aberrant conduction as the cause of hypotension, strengthening the link between the regular monomorphic wide complex tachycardia and the severe hypotension/dizziness. Normal electrolytes and the reduced likelihood of flecainide proarrhythmia further consolidate arrhythmia-related hypotension as the leading diagnosis, so confidence is increased from 0.85 to 0.90.

The laboratory physician analysis notes that normal electrolytes and absence of structural heart disease evidence make flecainide proarrhythmia less likely, although it cannot be excluded without drug levels and echocardiography. The drug history and marked QRS prolongation (180 ms) still keep this a credible alternative, but the expert opinion reduces the confidence from 0.72 to 0.55.

The ECG confirms a tachyarrhythmia as the likely cause of hypotension, and normal electrolytes reduce metabolic triggers. The prominent cardiac history and flecainide exposure make non-cardiac dizziness very unlikely.
